



STRONGER AFTER THE STORM 

IIFL FINANCE LIMITED 

INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT **2024-25** 

# STRONGER AFTER THE STORM 

Every storm tests the mettle of those who face it, and FY 2024-25 was a defining trial by fire for IIFL Finance. We were hit by a storm on three fronts - regulatory embargo on our gold loan business, curbs over microfinance lending (MFIN reduced lenders per borrower to three, capped total borrower indebtedness, etc.) and Income Tax raids on our offices in January. These headwinds brought unprecedented challenges that shook our journey. Yet, like all storms, this one too passed. Challenges may shake the path, but they do not break the spirit. And with the clearing skies comes clarity—uncertainty, too, has an expiry date. 

How did we manage to sail safely through the storm? We anchored ourselves firmly in our core values of fairness, integrity and transparency. With unwavering resolve, we navigated through turbulent waters, transforming adversity into opportunity. The RBI embargo on our gold loans lasted little over six months and we managed to stay above water during the turmoil. All our branches remained operational and we continued to engage with all our stakeholders - customers, bankers, regulators seamlessly. There were zero job losses, no salary reductions during these testing times, demonstrating our commitment to the well-being of our people. We addressed the queries of our lenders in a transparent manner, paying back over ` 18,000 Crores to them. We also revamped our processes, policies, systems and resources to ensure a smooth return to business as usual – without imposition of any penalty or limitations. Even in these tumultuous times, we managed to raise US$ 152 Million via a fully subscribed rights issue, a clear signal of continued investor confidence in our Company. While the MFIN regulations have affected performance of microfinance companies, we believe these reforms are grounded in good intent, with a strong focus on safeguarding borrowers’ interests. 

Emerging from the storm, we are sharper, more focused, and fiercely determined. 

Our governance frameworks have been reinforced, risk controls recalibrated (with strengthening of board, management team and compliance function), and our bond of trust with customers reaffirmed. The embers of disruption have ignited a renewed passion to innovate, grow prudently, and build a future-ready enterprise. 

The theme “Stronger After the Storm” is more than a theme — it is the story of our journey from challenge to triumph, from disruption to resurgence. It embodies the resilience that defines us, the hard-earned lessons we have embraced, and the strategic clarity that now shapes our path ahead. 

As we chart the path ahead, our strengthened foundations empower us to seize new opportunities, especially in high-potential MSME lending space, supported by a powerful phygital model and cutting-edge digital infrastructure. 

The storm has tested us, but it has also made us stronger. Today, IIFL Finance stands stronger, ready to navigate the horizon with confidence, conviction, and an unshakeable commitment to create lasting value. 

## **In Memoriam** 

# Mr. Kranti Sinha 

(Independent Director, IIFL Group) 

### **(1942–2025)** 

“A steady compass of wisdom and integrity, Mr. Sinha left behind not just footprints — but firm foundations.” 

It is with deep respect and profound sadness that we remember and honor Mr. Kranti Sinha, whose passing has left a void in the heart of IIFL Finance and the broader BFSI community. 

A veteran with decades of leadership in the insurance and housing finance sectors, Mr. Sinha joined the Board of IIFL Group as an Independent Director in 2005. Over the years, his principled and insightful contributions helped shape our governance architecture, refine our long-term strategy, and build enduring trust with stakeholders. 

He served on our Board with distinction until his retirement in 2019 from IIFL Finance and in 2023 from the Board of IIFL Home Finance, after which he remained a respected well-wisher and advisor. 

More than a Board Member, Mr. Sinha was a mentor and guide to Mr. Nirmal Jain, Founder & Managing Director, and Mr. R. Venkataraman, Joint Managing Director. His wisdom illuminated many of our most important decisions—from navigating regulatory transitions to deepening financial inclusion. 

Mr. Sinha believed in responsible innovation and disciplined growth. He championed ethical lending, strong risk frameworks, and outreach to underbanked communities—values that remain foundational to our mission. 

#### Reflections 

“Mr. Sinha’s clarity of thought and unwavering principles were an inspiration to me personally and to all of us at IIFL.” 

**Nirmal Jain,** Founder & Managing Director 

“He brought a calm strength and deep wisdom to every discussion. We are better because of his presence.” 

**R. Venkataraman,** Joint Managing Director 

We extend our deepest condolences to his family and loved ones. 

His legacy—of governance, integrity, and purpose-driven leadership—will always remain a part of IIFL’s DNA. 

May his soul rest in peace. 

# ABOUT THIS REPORT 

## REPORTING SCOPE AND BOUNDARY 

The Integrated Annual Report (“Report”) for FY 2024-25 presents a holistic narrative of IIFL Finance Limited’s journey in delivering on its purpose. It articulates how the Company (hereinafter referred to as ‘IIFL’, ‘we’, ‘our Company’, or ‘the Company’) creates sustainable value for its stakeholders—including customers, shareholders, lenders, regulators, employees, and society at large. This commitment forms the cornerstone of our value creation story and highlights our broader impact beyond financial performance. In addition to financial metrics, the Report offers insights into our non-financial performance, key risks and opportunities, strategic priorities, and sustainability initiatives. It also details the governance and risk management frameworks that support and strengthen our overall performance. 

The Report covers the primary activities of the Company, including its subsidiaries and other investments where the Company has financial control and significant influence. 

## REPORTING PERIOD 

This Report is prepared for the period from  April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025, in alignment with the Company’s financial reporting cycle ending on March 31, 2025. It also incorporates key developments occurring after the reporting period and up to the date of Board meeting, i.e., May 8, 2025, where the statutory reports were placed for the approval. 



# REPORTING PRINCIPLES AND FRAMEWORK 

This Report has been prepared in alignment with the principles of the International Integrated Reporting Framework (IIRC), while also adhering to the disclosure requirements under the SEBI-prescribed Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) format and the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards. The financial information presented herein complies with the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 (including the rules framed thereunder), the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, 2021, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

### **WHO WE ARE** 

# CONTRIBUTORS TO INDIA’S PROGRESS 

Over the past three decades, IIFL Finance Limited has solidified its stature as one of India’s foremost non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). Renowned for its unwavering commitment to integrity, transparency, and customer-centricity, our Company offers innovative, tailored financial solutions that foster inclusive growth and financial empowerment across the nation. 

Headquartered in Mumbai, IIFL Finance has transformed into a diversified financial services powerhouse. Its expansive product portfolio includes home loans, gold loans, MSME loans, microfinance, and capital market financingaddressing the unique needs of both retail and corporate clients. With a robust national presence and an unwavering focus on innovation, IIFL Finance continues to be a catalyst in broadening access to finance. 

By prioritizing the underserved and underbanked segments of the society, 

IIFL Finance is making a significant contribution to India’s progress toward financial inclusion, ensuring that financial services reach every corner of the country. 

Complementing our core activities, the IIFL Foundation serves as the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) arm of the IIFL Group. Established in 2014, the Foundation has been actively addressing critical social challenges through its strategic focus on HELP — Health, Education & Environment, Livelihood, and Poverty Alleviation. 

Through the Foundation, we extend our purpose beyond businessdriving meaningful change and contributing to the creation of a more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable society. Our initiatives reflect a deep commitment to uplifting communities and empowering individuals, reinforcing our belief that true growth is measured not only in profits, but in the positive impact we create. 



## **OUR VISION** 

To be the most respected financial services company in India. Not necessarily the largest or most profitable.

# SEAMLESSLY ALIGNED 

## **OUR SUBSIDIARIES** 

Our subsidiaries — IIFL Home Finance and IIFL Samasta Finance Limited - are integral to expanding IIFL Finance’s retail lending footprint. By strategically operating across key sectors including home loans and microfinance loans, they significantly amplify our Company’s capacity to serve a diverse range of borrowers, while further solidifying our presence in the market. 



### IIFL HOME FINANCE LIMITED 





IIFL Home Finance Limited (IIFL HFL) is India’s leading affordable housing finance company, championing homeownership for first-time buyers in the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Lower Income Groups (LIG). It is dedicated to promoting inclusivity, women empowerment, and sustainable development. With over 370 branches across 20 states and union territories, and an advanced IT infrastructure, the company ensures a seamless and accessible loan process for those seeking to fulfill their housing aspirations. 

### IIFL SAMASTA FINANCE LIMITED 





IIFL Samasta Finance Limited, a prominent NBFC-MFI, is dedicated to providing microfinance solutions to individuals in rural and semi-urban regions. Through its commitment to financial inclusion and the promotion of grassroots entrepreneurship, the company plays a pivotal role in empowering underserved communities, driving socio-economic progress, and fostering sustainable development.

## **OUR CUSTOMER SUCCESS STORY** 



### Tarun Sundar spark: Powering MSME growth with gold 

Tarun Sundar Lal Mehta, a successful textile business owner in Surat, is working tirelessly to fulfil his son’s dream of becoming a doctor. 

But things weren’t always so hopeful and bright when Tarun faced a loss of `₹27 Lakhs in his new business venture. Refusing to give up, he turned to IIFL Finance for a gold loan to start over. 

The funding helped Tarun get back on track financially, but that was not all. As his success showed promise for further growth, he took a business loan to expand and turn his and his family’s dreams into reality.

# AFFORDABLE HOME LOANS 

IIFL Finance, through its subsidiary, IIFL Home Finance Limited, is committed to promoting homeownership among underserved segments by offering affordable housing finance solutions. Backed by an extensive phygital network and a profound understanding of customer requirements, the company ensures seamless, inclusive, and efficient access to formal housing credit. It primarily serves first-time homebuyers from the economically weaker sections and low-income group segments, with a strong emphasis on non-metro and semi-urban regions.

# GOLD LOANS 

Our Company offers small-ticket, short-duration gold loans, providing individuals and small businesses with immediate access to liquidity against their gold jewellery. Backed by a pan-India network of over 2,833 branches, IIFL Finance ensures swift, transparent, and digitally enabled disbursals. To further enhance customer convenience, we also offer a ‘Gold Loan at Home’ service—delivering a secure, paperless, and hassle-free loan experience right at the customer’s doorstep, eliminating the need to visit a branch. Designed to meet the financial needs of underserved communities, the gold loan offering strengthens economic resilience by providing timely credit support.

# **KEY DEVELOPMENTS DURING FY 2024-25** 

## RBI LIFTS OPERATIONAL RESTRICTION 



The Reserve Bank of India lifted the regulatory embargo on gold loan disbursements in September 2024, following the successful implementation of corrective measures by IIFL Finance, enabling our Company to resume normal operations and rebuild growth momentum. 

## STRONG RECOVERY POST-EMBARGO 

Following the lifting of RBI’s embargo, we rapidly revived our gold loan business, demonstrating strong customer loyalty and operational resilience. 

## FOCUS ON COMPLIANCE AND RISK MITIGATION 

Post-embargo, our Company enhanced risk governance, audit mechanisms, and auction protocols to align closely with RBI’s regulations. 

## SHARP AUM RECOVERY POST-EMBARGO 

Gold loan AUM surged 40% quarter-on-quarter in Q4 FY25, rebounding to ` 21,022 Crores. This highlights the strong brand franchise and customer stickiness post-compliance correction. 

## EMPLOYEE RETENTION AMIDST DISRUPTION 

Despite operational disruptions during the embargo period, Our Company maintained full workforce stability, undertaking no layoffs, salary reductions, or branch closures, reaffirming our commitment to employee welfare and organizational resilience.

# MSME LOANS 

We provide secured and unsecured business loans to self-employed individuals, micro-business owners, and small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Focused on empowering businesses across urban and semi-urban regions, our Company offers timely financing solutions for working capital, business expansion, and asset creation, backed by a robust underwriting framework and tech-enabled processes. Our Company leverages advanced data analytics, proprietary apps, and fintech partnerships to deliver fully paperless, cash-flow backed loans with instant approvals and seamless disbursals. With a strong emphasis on speed, convenience, and rigorous risk management, IIFL Finance’s digital lending platform enables underserved businesses to access timely credit, fostering entrepreneurial growth and supporting financial inclusion.

## STRATEGIC PORTFOLIO REBALANCING

## STRENGTHENING RISK MANAGEMENT 

Intensify borrower profiling, early-stage delinquency tracking, and credit discipline to safeguard portfolio performance.

## Dear Stakeholders, 

It is my privilege to present to you IIFL Finance’s Integrated Annual Report for FY 2024–25. This has been a year of transformation, learning, and resolute action—one that truly embodies our theme, Stronger after the Storm. The regulatory intervention on our gold loan business in March 2024 tested our agility, integrity, and institutional maturity. While the Reserve Bank of India’s embargo temporarily restrained us from disbursing new gold loans, it also served as a critical opportunity to recalibrate our approach to risk and compliance. 

We met the moment with urgency, clarity, and integrity—swiftly enacting corrective measures, elevating our internal systems, and recalibrating our priorities to meet the demands of the future. The completion of the special audit and our return to regular operations stand as a testament to our unwavering commitment to regulatory compliance. 

More than a course correction, this journey has been a catalyst— fortifying our foundations, sharpening our focus, and igniting a renewed determination to build back better. We emerged more resilient, more responsible, and more deeply aligned with our enduring mission: to expand the reach of financial inclusion and create lasting impact for the communities we serve. 

At the heart of our mission lies a deep commitment to broadening the reach of organized lending across the country. Our Company started with the dedication to serving the underserved—those often left behind by traditional financial systems—through an inclusive suite of loan products tailored to real, everyday needs. About 93% of our loans are for productive purposes, empowering borrowers to invest in their futures—funding home construction or repairs, educating their children, supporting agricultural activity, or fueling the growth of small 

businesses and service enterprises. We walk shoulder-to-shoulder with MSMEs, the backbone of India’s employment engine, through agile, tech-driven lending solutions. In our journey spanning three decades, we have touched the lives of more than 8 Million customers, most of whom have been grassroots economy builders. 

Currently, about 86% of our customers are from the economically weaker section, with annual income of `₹0-3 Lakhs. They now dare to dream big and pursue aspirations once thought out of reach. For many, our support has meant liberation from the exploitative grip of informal moneylenders, offering a path to dignity, stability, and financial empowerment. With all our wheels spinning and engine roaring, we are ready to accelerate innovation and drive forward at full speed. We continue to actively support the resilient and rising credit demand of India’s small businesses—driven by 

Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 

18 

` 

<mark>Strategic Review</mark> 

the same mission that has guided us from the start: to democratize access to finance and build a more inclusive economy. About 84% of our branches are in non-metro areas and cater to the underserved populace of the country, taking formal credit deeper into the hinterlands of India. 91.27% of our unsecured MSME digital loans given are of less than ` 1 Million, breathing life into small ventures, propelling them toward greatness. 

## Macro landscape: A pillar of support 

India is undergoing a paradigm shift—one that goes beyond cyclical economic growth and instead embraces structural transformation. The national aspiration of Viksit Bharat 2047, aimed at shaping India into a developed economy, is built on four foundational pillars: inclusive development, digital empowerment, world-class infrastructure, and sustainable livelihoods. These priorities are steadily reshaping the contours of the financial ecosystem. 

In this long-term journey, financial inclusion is not just a policy goal—it is a strategic imperative. As the nation accelerates its push towards formalization of and equitable access to credit, NBFCs and microfinance institutions have emerged as critical enablers. Their ability to serve those traditionally overlooked by mainstream financial systems—such as small traders, self-employed individuals, women entrepreneurs, and informal households—makes them vital partners in India’s developmental blueprint. 

## Our performance: Strengthening core, reviving momentum 

FY 2024–25 was a year of reflection and realignment. Against the backdrop of regulatory intervention in our gold loan business, our overall growth remained subdued. The Company’s consolidated AUM declined marginally by 1%, reflecting the temporary pause in gold loan disbursements for a significant part of the year. 

Despite this softness in topline metrics, our balance sheet remained 

fundamentally strong. Asset quality was well contained, with Gross NPA at 2.2% and Net NPA at 1.0%, underscoring the effectiveness of our credit and risk management frameworks. Liquidity buffers were maintained at prudent levels throughout the year, ensuring seamless operations and the ability to meet all financial obligations with confidence. 

Encouragingly, the second half of the year marked a turning point. With the embargo lifted and corrective actions firmly in place, business momentum improved across key segments. Disbursements gathered pace in home loans, MSME finance, digital lending, and gold loans—driven by renewed customer confidence, enhanced governance protocols, and the disciplined execution of our branch-led model. 

This performance highlights the underlying resilience of our model and the agility of our teams. With stronger institutional focus, tighter controls, and restored momentum, we are well poised to return to a trajectory of sustainable growth in the coming year. 

## Our ESG commitment: Responsible growth, inclusive impact 

We continued to advance our ESG agenda with a long-term, institution-wide perspective. On the environmental front, we accelerated paperless operations, energy-efficient practices, and green loan offerings— aligning with our commitment to responsible lending and climateconscious growth. Socially, our focus on inclusive development remained strong. We retained our entire workforce through the year, despite operational disruptions, reaffirming our belief in protecting livelihoods. Through our flagship CSR initiative Sakhiyon Ki Baadi, we continued to empower out-of-school girls in Rajasthan with access to basic numeracy and literacy skills, and life skills. On governance, we responded to regulatory expectations with urgency and transparency—further strengthening our internal controls and assurance frameworks. As we 

look ahead, our ESG commitments will remain central to how we grow— with integrity, inclusivity, and longterm impact. 

## Closing thoughts: The road ahead 

Resilience, reflection, and purposeful transformation have defined our recent journey. The challenges we navigated have not only strengthened our institutional core but also reinforced our commitment to ethical governance, stakeholder trust, and inclusive finance. We emerge from this phase more agile, more focused, and more aligned with our mission to empower underserved communities through responsible lending. 

With the reinstatement of our gold loan business and strong momentum across MSME, housing, and digital lending segments, we enter FY 2025–26 with renewed confidence. Backed by strengthened compliance, enhanced operational discipline, and robust customer demand, we are targeting a return to double-digit AUM growth. Our strategic imperatives are clear—drive sustainable expansion, deepen customer reach, and deliver long-term value with accountability and purpose. 

As I prepare to retire, I reflect with gratitude on the 17 years I have had the privilege to serve IIFL Finance. It has been a distinct opportunity to contribute to our shared vision and witness our growth and achievements first-hand. I am proud of the progress we have made together and confident that the strong foundation we have built will support continued success in the future. My best wishes to Nirmal, Venkat and team IIFL Finance for the future. I extend my heartfelt thanks to the board, management, staff, and stakeholders for their unwavering support throughout my tenure. I look forward to seeing this great organization flourish in the years ahead. . 

Warm Regards, 

# A. K. Purwar

## Dear Stakeholders, 

FY 2024–25 will be remembered as a defining chapter in the journey of IIFL Finance—a year of turbulence, tenacity, and transformation. The theme of this Annual Report— “Stronger After the Storm”—reflects not only the external challenges we weathered, but also the deep reserves of resilience we uncovered within. 

#### Weathering a perfect storm 

We encountered a confluence of unprecedented disruptions: a regulatory embargo on our gold loan business, systemic stress in the microfinance sector, an exceptional provision related to our AIF investment, and an extensive income tax search across offices and homes of key personnel. These events tested the very core of our institution. Yet, 

through it all, we remained steadfast— anchored in our values, powered by our people, and guided by our belief in India’s regulatory framework and long-term potential. 

#### A principled and decisive response 

When the Reserve Bank of India imposed temporary restrictions on our gold loan operations, we acted with urgency, transparency, and responsibility. We engaged constructively with the regulator, conducted a rigorous root cause analysis, and implemented robust internal and external audit frameworks. Our systems and controls were recalibrated to ensure full compliance with regulatory expectations. 

Importantly, we stood by our people— no branches were shut, no employees were laid off, and no salaries were cut. As disbursements resumed with enhanced safeguards and greater transparency, we recovered lost momentum within just 2-3 months. 

Our microfinance subsidiary also came under pressure due to sectorwide external shocks, resulting in elevated provisions and temporary losses in the second and third quarters. Yet, even during this period, we remained true to our mission— supporting vulnerable borrowers with empathy and flexibility. Our conservatively built balance sheet absorbed the impact and safeguarded the long-term sustainability of the business. 

Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 

20 

<mark>Strategic Review</mark> 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
`<br><!-- End of picture text -->

As we navigated these disruptions, an income tax search was initiated across the group. We extended full cooperation to authorities, providing complete access to records and systems. IIFL has always upheld the highest standards of compliance, governance, and transparency—and we remain firmly committed to these principles. 

## Performance rebounds as the storm subsides 

As the saying goes, “every storm runs out of wind”, the second half of the year saw a strong resurgence in performance: 

- Profit After Tax for FY25 stood at ` 578 Crores 

- Q4 PAT grew by 208% quarter-onquarter 

- Gold loan AUM rose 40% quarteron-quarter 

- Gross NPA improved to 2.2% 

- AUM grew 10% sequentially in Q4, with strong momentum across business lines 

Our credit ratings remained AA (Stable) from CRISIL, reflecting the resilience of our balance sheet and the strength of our fundamentals. Our shareholders reaffirmed their confidence by fully subscribing to our ` 1,272 Crores rights issue, bolstering capital at a critical juncture. 

Beyond the numbers, FY25 was a year of internal renewal. We streamlined operations, fortified our governance framework, upgraded our risk architecture, and realigned our strategy for long-term, sustainable growth. 

## Building for the future 

As we step into FY26, our focus is on acceleration and innovation. We are investing meaningfully in AI-powered credit models, predictive risk engines, compliance automation, and fully digital customer journeys. These are not incremental improvements—they are foundational enablers of the future of finance. 

We are also scaling our MSME and small business lending platform— an engine of inclusive growth and national resilience. Leveraging our pan-India branch network, advanced technology stack, and deep customer insights, we aim to build a high quality, scalable lending franchise serving India’s entrepreneurial backbone. 

## A tribute to Mr. Arun Purwar 

This year also marks the retirement of our Chairman, Mr. A. K. Purwar, after more than 17 years of extraordinary service. His wisdom, integrity, and strategic guidance have shaped our institution and strengthened our governance. During the RBI embargo, he stood by the Company with calm leadership and unshakeable support. While he now steps down from formal responsibilities, he remains a mentor, guide, and source of inspiration. On behalf of the entire IIFL family, I extend our heartfelt gratitude and deepest respect. 

## Governance before growth 

If one principle has defined our journey this year, it is this: Governance before Growth. At IIFL, we believe that sustainable growth must be rooted in integrity, transparency, and regulatory 

alignment. Growth is vital—but only when built on the foundations of trust and long-term purpose. 

Amidst the disruptions, our ESG initiatives continued undeterred. Our flagship education program reached over 32,000 girl children in Rajasthan’s rural districts, alongside other impactful interventions in water access, women’s empowerment, and skill development. Remarkably, during the embargo, our employees voluntarily took on additional responsibilities to contribute more— demonstrating the true spirit of IIFL. 

## Stronger. Sharper. Clearer. 

FY 2024-25 was not just a storm—it was a crucible. Moreover, we have emerged from it stronger, sharper, and more focused. Our foundation is more resilient, our leadership more aligned, and our strategy clearer than ever. 

To our customers, regulators, investors, and employees—thank you. Your trust has been our anchor in turbulent times. As we move ahead, that trust remains our greatest asset—and our most solemn responsibility. 

Warm regards, 

# Nirmal Jain

### **OUR STRENGTHS** 

# RESILIENT ACROSS STORMS 

## **DIVERSIFIED PRODUCT PORTFOLIO CATERING TO A WIDE CUSTOMER BASE** 

We offer a comprehensive range of secured and unsecured lending products, including home loans, gold loans, business loans, microfinance, MSME secured loans, MSME unsecured loans, supply chain finance, construction and real estate finance and capital market financing. These products are tailored to meet the needs of diverse customer segments—from salaried individuals and self-employed professionals to micro-entrepreneurs and rural borrowers. This broad portfolio enables us to expand our reach, mitigate asset concentration risk, and maintain a steady income mix across market conditions.

Broader outreach 

PSL alignment 

## **DIVERSIFIED FUNDING SOURCES AND STRONG CREDIT PROFILE** 

We access funding through a healthy mix of public and private sector banks, development finance institutions, securitization, and capital markets. We have successfully raised long-term debt and equity capital over the years. Our credit ratings—AA/Stable by CRISIL and ICRA—reflect our robust financial position and prudent liability management. 

#### **Impact** 

   - Expanding with financial prudence 

   - Resilient during volatility 

- Reduced asset concentration risk 

## **SUSTAINED ASSET QUALITY** 

Our asset quality is underpinned by our rigorous credit underwriting practices, customized risk-based pricing, and disciplined collections. With approximately 80.5% of our loan book backed by tangible security, we have maintained a GNPA of 2.2% and NNPA of 1.0% as of March 31, 2025, demonstrating strong portfolio resilience across economic cycles. 

#### **Impact** 

Strong risk-adjusted returns 

Consistent portfolio health across cycles 

## **STRONG PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL FOOTPRINT** 

With a presence in 28 states and union territories through over 4,900+ branches and service points, our widespread physical infrastructure is augmented by our digital capabilities. Our branch-led sourcing, supported by tech-driven customer onboarding and servicing, allows us to deliver loans efficiently even in rural and semi-urban areas, creating a competitive advantage in last-mile credit delivery.

## **STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT** 

# STAKEHOLDER INTEREST FIRST 

To us, stakeholder engagement is the foundation of our sustained success and growth. Engagement with a diverse spectrum of stakeholders helps cultivate deep relationships with them. ## **MATERIALITY ASSESSMENT** 

# FOCUSING ON WHAT MATTERS MOST 

During FY 2023-24, we conducted our second materiality assessment to prioritize the most important areas for channeling our resources and making strategic alignments. This exercise enabled us to determine priority areas where our strategic efforts and resource allocations would yield the greatest impact. It focused on identifying the most significant economic, environmental, and social impacts—both actual and potential—including those related to human rights. 

The assessment adhered to the GRI Standards 2021 and was enriched by insights from global benchmarks such as SASB and MSCI, ensuring relevance to our business model. Key material topics were shortlisted through comparative analysis and subsequently prioritized through structured engagements with stakeholders, senior leadership, and the Board. 

Post this exercise, the scope of our material priorities has broadened to include human rights, diversity and inclusion, and customer financial protection—reflecting our growing commitment to responsible business practices. A robust monitoring framework supports our progress tracking, leveraging defined goals and KPIs to evaluate impact. Regular 

reviews facilitate early identification of gaps and corrective actions. Lessons learned—especially the need for data-centric governance and sustained stakeholder dialogue—are actively embedded into our operating procedures, reinforcing alignment with our Company’s long-term strategic vision.

# **THREE LINES OF DEFENCE MODEL** 

Our risk management is deeply embedded in our organizational culture and operational fabric. We diligently monitor and manage potential threats to ensure business resilience amid evolving uncertainties. Our approach prioritizes compliance with regulatory requirements and global best practices, while promoting a strong culture of risk awareness and accountability across all levels of the organization. Through proactive identification and mitigation of risks, we safeguard stakeholder interests and support our long-term growth trajectory. 

To institutionalize this approach, we have adopted the ‘Three Lines of Defence’ model. This structured framework delineates clear roles and responsibilities to ensure comprehensive risk oversight: 



<!-- Start of picture text -->
Line of Defence Responsibility<br>1 st Line Business & Operational Management – Own and manage risks<br>2 nd Line Risk & Compliance – Oversight, guidance and support<br>3 rd Line Internal Audit – Independent assurance<br><!-- End of picture text -->

## OPERATIONAL RISK GOVERNANCE: 

## STRUCTURED. ACCOUNTABLE. PREVENTIVE. 





IIFL Finance’s operational risk governance is not reactive—it is preventative, structured, and deeply embedded in our culture of accountability. Anchored by a proactive review system, we ensure that risks are not only identified and mitigated, but also transformed into opportunities for improvement. With dedicated oversight bodies, clearly defined responsibilities, and realtime reporting mechanisms, we drive operational integrity and organizational resilience.

### **MARKET OPPORTUNITY** 

# RIDING THE WAVE OF FINANCIAL INCLUSION 

## **UNDERSERVED MSME SECTOR** 

India’s MSME sector continues to face significant credit access challenges. In the MSME landscape, despite contributing around 30% to India’s GDP and employing over 110 million individuals, a significant credit gap remains. According to NITI Aayog (2024), only 19% of MSME credit demand was met by formal financial channels, leaving an estimated ` 80 Lakh Crores gap. 

This substantial credit gap presents a compelling opportunity for NBFCs like IIFL Finance to expand their reach by offering tailored, tech-enabled lending solutions.

MSME credit demand addressed through formal channels 

Source: MSME credit rises to 20%, $94.92 bn gap remains: NITI Aayog - Fibre2Fashion 

## **BANK-NBFC PARTNERSHIP MODEL** 

The Bank–NBFC co-lending model offers NBFCs like IIFL Finance a scalable opportunity to expand credit delivery without significantly increasing balance sheet risk. According to RBI data, co-lending portfolios between banks and NBFCs have grown substantially, with public sector banks’ exposure crossing ` 11,497 Crores in FY 2023-24. This model allows NBFCs to leverage their reach into underserved markets while banks provide low-cost capital— creating a win-win for credit expansion.

# **ROBUST WORKING CAPITAL DEMAND** 

India’s corporate sector is poised for substantial growth, with Moody’s estimating that 16 of the 23 rated non-financial companies will require between US$ 70–100 Billion annually over the next two years. This capital is earmarked for capacity expansion, inorganic growth, refinancing, working capital needs, and shareholder payments. The surge in capital requirements is driven by strong consumption growth, high-capacity utilization, and ongoing infrastructure investments. NBFCs having a diversified lending portfolio and deep market penetration, are well-positioned to meet this escalating demand.

# **UNDER-PENETRATION OF GOLD LOANS, HOUSING LOANS AND MICROFINANCE** 

India’s secured and inclusive finance segments remain significantly underpenetrated. The organized gold loan market stood at ` 7.1 Lakh Crores in FY 2023-24, with a penetration of just 5.6% despite widespread household gold ownership. In housing finance, individual loans touched ` 33.5 Lakh Crores by Q2 FY25, but regional disparities—particularly in Eastern and rural India—highlight untapped demand. Similarly, the microfinance sector serves over 6.6 Crores unique borrowers, yet remains underserved in tier-III and IV markets. NBFCs having deep rural reach and proven expertise across all three segments are strongly positioned to scale lending in these highpotential categories through a compliance-first, tech-enabled approach.

# **BUSINESS CONTINUITY DURING THE RESTRICTION PERIOD** 



## EMPLOYEE RETENTION 

Maintained complete workforce stability with no layoffs, salary cuts, or branch closures, demonstrating strong commitment to employee well-being even during regulatory disruptions 



## CUSTOMER RELATIONS 

Maintained transparent communication with gold loan customers, enabling the orderly liquidation of over 60% of assets and the safe return of jewellery to 1.2 Million customers—preserving trust and strengthening long-term relationships 



## BANK AND LENDER RELATIONS 

Timely repayments of over US$ 2.2 Billion were ensured to banking partners, reinforcing our Company’s strong repayment discipline and credibility. Also, proactively engaged with banking partners and NBFC lenders to share audit outcomes, regulatory updates, and operational readiness. 



## INVESTOR CONFIDENCE 

Maintained consistent communication with key investors and analysts through timely disclosures and strategic updates. This proactive engagement was instrumental in reinforcing investor confidence, with prominent institutional investor Fairfax reaffirming its trust by participating in both equity and bond issuances post-embargo. 



## CAPITAL AND LIQUIDITY 

Maintained strong liquidity and further strengthened our capital position by raising US$ 152 Million through a fully subscribed rights issue and securing an additional US$ 1.1 Billion in funding—ensuring uninterrupted operations and reflecting continued investor confidence in our Company. 



## CREDIT RATING 

Maintained AA credit rating (CRISIL) throughout the restriction period with no downgrade, reflecting robust capitalization and confidence in the governance and remedial actions undertaken.

# PARTNERSHIPS / COLLABORATIONS WITH TECH ECOSYSTEM 





Recognizing the value of collaborative innovation, IIFL Finance has forged strategic alliances with leading technology providers, cloud enablers, and fintech partners. These partnerships have supported co-lending integrations, real-time API connectivity, cloud scalability, and AI-driven automation—strengthening our Company’s position as a digitally empowered NBFC. Notably, the collaboration with Azure and specialized vendors has helped scale digital infrastructure and security resilience. 







# GEN AI ADOPTION ALIGNED TO BUSINESS STRATEGY 





In line with our innovation-led roadmap, we have piloted Generative AI applications and internal operations. The use of Gen AI supports and improves employee efficiency—delivering tangible impact across service quality and cost optimization. These pilots are being progressively aligned with business processes to institutionalize automation and strengthen competitive agility. 

# LEVERAGING TECHNOLOGY FOR BRANCH SECURITY 





To ensure safe and compliant operations across our vast branch network, our Company leverages advanced surveillance systems, access control solutions, and digitally monitored vault security for its gold loan operations. Integration of techdriven security protocols within the core infrastructure reinforces customer confidence and enhances regulatory adherence, particularly in high-risk geographies. 

# STABLE AND SECURE TECH SETUP 





Built on a robust Azure-based cloud foundation, our Company’s technology infrastructure is designed for resilience, agility, and scalability. With ISO27001 and ISO22301 certifications in place, our Company ensures business continuity, information security, and real-time performance monitoring across systems. Regular audits, vulnerability assessments, and a 24x7 automated SOC further reinforce our commitment to a secure digital environment.

# **CYBERSECURITY: FORTIFYING TRUST IN THE DIGITAL AGE** 

In an increasingly digital ecosystem, where the sanctity of data and digital trust determines business credibility, IIFL Finance has placed cybersecurity at the core of its technological strategy. Our Company’s multi-layered cybersecurity framework not only protects sensitive customer and business data but also ensures compliance, operational resilience, and stakeholder confidence. By embracing global standards and deploying proactive measures, we continue to strengthen our digital fortifications and safeguard our expanding digital footprint. 



## KEY CYBERSECURITY PRACTICES AND ENHANCEMENTS 



- Sustained ISO27001 Certification and initiated journey towards version migration from v2013 to v2022 

   - Strategic partnership with Data Security Council of India (DSCI) for cyber security and data privacy initiatives 

- Initiation of Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) implementation for enhanced security by continuous verification, minimizing risks from unauthorized users and devices 

   - Implementation of database activity monitoring solution 

   - Automation of tabletop cybersecurity drills to enhance security awareness and improve incident response readiness 

- Enhancement and automation of 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) services to enable rapid security incident detection and immediate response 

- Sustained ISO22301 Certification for Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) 



## CERTIFICATIONS AND ACCOLADES 



- ISO 27001 Certification version upgradation from v2013 to v2022, demonstrating robust Information Security Management System (ISMS) practices to protect sensitive customer and organizational data

## **ENVIRONMENT** 

# DRIVING GROWTH WITH A SUSTAINABLE VISION 



Environmental responsibility is integral to our business ethos. We are committed to reducing our carbon footprint through energyefficient operations, waste minimization, and sustainable financing. By embedding environmental stewardship into our strategy and embracing innovative technologies, we strive to create lasting value for our stakeholders while contributing to a greener, more sustainable future. 

Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 

70 

` 

<mark>Strategic Review</mark> 

# **Key challenges** 

# **Our response** 

- With expanding branch operations and digital infrastructure, managing Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions—particularly from electricity consumption—posed a significant challenge 

- As a financial services Company operating in leased premises, direct control over water discharge and treatment was limited. A significant portion of water was discharged untreated into municipal systems 

- Growth in digital operations led to rising e-waste (computers, servers, batteries) and residual paper waste from onboarding and servicing operations 

- Indirect emissions such as business travel, procurement, and vendor-related emissions were not formally tracked, limiting full impact visibility 

- Ensuring structured and standardized environmental management across key operational hubs while aligning with global sustainability benchmarks 

- Adopted Tata Green Tariff at the Mumbai office, achieved LEED Gold Certification for the Gurugram office building, and implemented LED lighting with smart sensors to enhance energy efficiency 

- Installed rainwater harvesting, sewage treatment systems and deployed aerators, water softeners and recycled water setups for secondary use like flushing and gardening at key offices 

- Partnered with certified vendors for responsible recycling of e-waste. Introduced bamboo-based tissue paper and digitalized recruitment, onboarding, and customer servicing to reduce paper usage 

- Initiated Scope 3 emission mapping processes for travel and IT assets to enhance transparency and accountability 

- We obtained ISO 14001:2015 certification for our offices in Mumbai, Thane, and Bangalore, adopting a globally recognized framework to enhance our environmental management system, ensure compliance, promote resource efficiency, and drive continuous improvement

# HUMARA KUTUMB 

Humara Kutumb is IIFL Home Finance Limited’s flagship CSR initiative focused on advancing sustainable and green self-construction practices among economically weaker section and low-income group households. The project provides technical support and financial assistance to help borrowers secure green building certifications for their self-constructed homes. Through this initiative, homeowners are empowered to adopt climate-resilient and resource-efficient construction practices, improving long-term affordability and environmental impact. 

The project also includes the development of demo houses in key geographies to serve as live models of green, affordable construction. These demo units are intended to educate local communities, masons, and other stakeholders about sustainable building techniques and certification benefits. The program aligns with national priorities on housing for all and environmental sustainability, while also contributing to IIFL’s broader ESG goals.

# PROMOTING GREEN HOUSING THROUGH SUSTAINABLE FINANCE 



Through our housing finance subsidiary, we are advancing India’s green transition by offering preferential financing for certified eco-friendly homes. As of FY 2024–25, over 26,358 green housing units have been funded, contributing to measurable climate outcomes including 24,317 MWh of annual energy savings, 1,401 ML of water savings, and 22,371 tonnes of CO2e offset. These efforts are supported by initiatives like Green Value Partnership (GVP) and technical collaborations with development institutions to mainstream sustainable construction in the affordable housing sector. 

# SMART WATER STEWARDSHIP 



Our offices are equipped with water-efficient infrastructure, including aerators, water softeners, and an 8,000-litre STP at our Gurugram office. Treated water is reused for landscaping and nonpotable applications, reducing freshwater withdrawal and discharge. Additionally, rainwater harvesting systems and drainage chambers are in place to optimize water use and reduce environmental impact, reinforcing our responsible water stewardship approach.

As part of our CSR initiatives, IIFL Home Finance Limited released Green Handbook Volume II, a comprehensive guide aimed at promoting sustainable self-construction practices in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. # SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT: MEASURING WHAT MATTERS 



Impact is meaningful only when it leads to measurable, lasting change in the lives of people. Guided by this principle, IIFL Foundation adopts a structured social impact assessment framework that combines strategic planning, stakeholder consultations, and robust monitoring and evaluation. 

One of the key programs assessed in FY 2024–25 was Sakhiyon Ki Baadi, which has expanded from 100 centers in 2016 to over 1,100+ learning hubs, reaching more than 32,000 girls across 15 districts at IIFL Group level. A third-party evaluation revealed: 

- 94% of educators confirmed expanded reach into underserved areas 

- 97% of students showed increased interest in learning 

- 77% of students reported better social interaction and classroom participation 

- 96% of educators improved their digital skills 

- 32% of educators reported enhanced household income due to economic participation 

- 68% of students demonstrated notable academic improvement 

These findings not only validate the program’s impact but also inform future enhancements. Through continuous assessment, each initiative is fine-tuned to maximize its value and effectiveness—ensuring that every action creates real, measurable progress. 









# METHODOLOGICAL INSIGHTS 





The impact of the Sakhiyon Ki Baadi initiative was assessed through an independent third-party study conducted by KPMG India, guided by the OECD-DAC evaluation framework. The evaluation followed a mixed-method approach, combining quantitative surveys and qualitative tools such as in-depth interviews and focus group discussions. Data was collected from 807 stakeholders, including 417 students, 293 parents, and 49 educators (Dakshas), along with implementing partners, school teachers, and local Government representatives across six districts. This comprehensive methodology enabled a holistic and credible evaluation of the program’s relevance, effectiveness, and sustainability.

## Bhavik Jain: Teaching transformed through technology 

Mr. Bhavik Jain, a Mathematics and Science teacher at Government Senior Secondary School, Badrana, embraced a new era of education with the integration of digital tools. Initially apprehensive, he faced challenges in operating the digital device provided to him under the program. However, with consistent training and support, his confidence grew. 

Today, Bhavik seamlessly integrates the digital platform into his teaching, making subjects more interactive and concepts easier for students to grasp. Beyond his lessons, he has noticed students voluntarily using the classroom TV to revise and explore content independently. Bhavik now sees technology as a game-changer in education and envisions its widespread adoption across rural schools.

# Ansh’s triumph over trauma 

Isolated, self-harming, and deeply distressed — this was the emotional world of young Ansh, who had lost his father and was being locked inside the house daily while his mother went to work. The absence of care and companionship pushed him into a shell of silence and destructive behavior. When he was brought to the shelter home, he was in class 4 and resisted everything — school, books, and even life itself. 

Through sustained counselling and dedicated care, Ansh slowly began to open up. His exceptional intelligence and curiosity were nurtured through one-on-one academic engagement and creative outlets like chess and dance. He began to thrive, developing leadership qualities and mentoring younger children at the home. Today, a student of class 9, Ansh dreams of becoming a veterinary doctor. He is focused, independent, and a source of hope for others around him. 

## **Empowerment journey :** 

Suffered severe emotional trauma and self-harm 

Now a motivated grade 9 student with a dream of becoming a vet 



# A star teacher’s journey with digital tools: Santosh Soni 

Santosh Soni, a veteran government school teacher in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, experienced a turning point in her teaching journey with the introduction of the Smartshala tools in 2022. After years of grappling with inadequate teaching materials and high administrative loads, she finally felt equipped to deliver quality education, through this program. 

With access to the Smartshala App, FLN TV device, and audio-based learning aids, her classroom underwent a remarkable shift. Lessons became more interactive, students lost their fear of subjects like mathematics, and learning outcomes began to improve tangibly. Her school’s environment became more joyful and productive. 

The transformation culminated with Santosh winning the coveted “Star Teacher Award” while her school was named a “Star School”. Her journey is now a beacon of hope for other rural educators. 

## **Empowerment journey :** 

Limited to government books and overwhelmed by admin duties 

Now a national award-winning educator inspiring digital learning in rural Rajasthan 



# Ashiq Hussain Najar: Learning to lead 

Ashiq, a determined youth from Drugmulla, Kupwara, enrolled in the IIFL Foundation-funded skill training program. With limited opportunities and formal education up to class 10, he pursued training with zeal. Upon completion, ashiq became an assistant trainer at the Skill Hub. His story reflects the power of opportunity to convert beneficiaries into future mentors.

From a limited education background 

Became a trainer, mentoring others in the same program

# **KEY CUSTOMER-FOCUSED INITIATIVES** 

## **Phygital delivery model** 

We continued to strengthen our unique phygital model that integrates our extensive branch presence with digital platforms. This hybrid approach ensures personalized service while enabling convenience and accessibility for customers across geographies. 

## **Paperless loan onboarding** 

To simplify and accelerate the borrowing experience, we enabled 100% paperless onboarding for home loans, business loans, and gold loans. This has significantly reduced processing time and improved customer satisfaction. 

## **IIFL Loans App and customer portal** 

Our self-service digital platforms empower customers to manage their loans end-to-end—view statements, make payments, raise service requests, and apply for top-ups—all from a single interface. 

## **Digital co-lending ecosystem** 

By integrating seamlessly with co-lending partners through API infrastructure, we offer customers faster credit access and wider product choices, while ensuring transparency and compliance.

# **OMNICHANNEL ENGAGEMENT FOR DEEPER CUSTOMER CONNECT** 

We employ a comprehensive multi-channel marketing strategy to engage customers and promote our financial offerings. Our outreach spans digital platforms, grassroots activations, and social media engagement, enabling us to connect effectively with a diverse and widespread customer base. 

## EXPANDING REACH THROUGH DIGITAL CHANNELS 

Our Company harnessed the power of digital tools like SMS and WhatsApp to communicate directly with our customers. These platforms enabled us to share campaign updates, personalized offers, and service reminders in real-time—ensuring faster, more relevant engagement. 

## ENGAGING AUDIENCES THROUGH SOCIAL STORYTELLING 

Social media became a powerful platform to inform, educate, and connect. We maintained an active presence on Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube, sharing relatable content that demystified gold loans and financial services. Using reels, short videos, and infographics, we reached younger, mobile-first audiences with simplified, regionalized narratives. YouTube, in particular, served as a platform for financial literacy—addressing evolving financial needs and enabling informed decision-making through accessible video content. 

## STRENGTHENING TRUST THROUGH ON-GROUND PRESENCE 

While digital drove convenience, our grassroots presence ensured familiarity and trust—especially in rural India. By participating in high-footfall local events such as melas and mandis, we created opportunities for face-to-face engagement, answered customer queries, and built lasting relationships. 

# **DIGITAL INTIATIVES** 

- Partnered with next-generation fintech lenders to expand offerings into business and supply chain finance, backed by risk-sharing arrangements and digitalized disbursals 

- Upgraded the IIFL Loans App, enhancing the customer experience with improved UI/UX, online top-ups, renewals, and faster EMI payments

# **MARKETING INITIATIVES** 

KEY MARKETING INITIATIVES DURING 2024-25 

## **Gold loan-focused initiatives** 

IIFL Finance strengthened its gold loan positioning through the Mahashakti Campaign, highlighting gold as a reliable financial lifeline during uncertain times. Tailored for rural and women borrowers, the campaign was amplified during festive seasons and Women’s Day to build emotional and cultural resonance. On-ground Gold Loan Melas and WhatsApp-led promotions were paired with referral tools to boost visibility and customer trust. 



## **Referral-driven campaigns** 

To scale organic customer acquisition and improve branchlevel engagement, IIFL Finance launched structured referral programs during the year. These included customer-facing referral campaigns as well as internal Referral Leagues at the branch level. Employees were encouraged to actively promote services within their communities, incentivizing both awareness and participation. These initiatives not only boosted lead generation but also helped instil trust, as referrals came from known and credible sources. The customers and employees were able to earn points and use them for various options like Vouchers, Gift Cards, Recharges and Bill Payments. 



## **Video-first content strategy** 

Recognizing the growing influence of visual content, IIFL Finance invested in a video-first storytelling approach. Short films and festival-themed reels were developed to emotionally connect with audiences and simplify financial concepts. These videos were deployed across Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube, helping to humanize loan offerings and increase engagement with a younger, digitally savvy demographic.

To streamline content production and maintain speed-to-market, IIFL Finance adopted an AI-enabled approach for creating marketing material. The AI tools ensured consistency in branding while accelerating the pace and responsiveness of the campaigns. 



# **Segment-specific targeting** 

Campaigns were carefully tailored to meet the unique needs of various customer segments. One key strategy focused on women, highlighting their increasing role as financial decision-makers. Similarly, small businesses were targeted through content that reflected their aspirations and showcased IIFL’s MSME lending support. 



# **Multi-channel customer engagement** 

A robust multi-channel strategy ensured wide outreach and deeper customer connection. Educational blogs, referral features, and interactive content enhanced digital engagement, while high-footfall rural mandis and melas enabled personal, trust-led conversations. This blend of digital and physical touchpoints helped IIFL Finance stay accessible, relatable, and responsive across its diverse customer base.

# **LEARNING & DEVELOPMENT** 

At IIFL Finance, employee development is a strategic priority, supported by highquality content, advanced technology, and strong project execution. Our commitment to learning begins on day one, with a fully digital 10-hour Induction Journey available in 10 regional languages. This comprehensive program covers functional, regulatory, and cultural aspects of onboarding, ensuring a seamless start for every new joiner. 

Induction at IIFL Finance is not a one-time event, but a springboard for continuous capability building. Following the digital induction, employees participate in virtual or classroom-based workshops for deeper functional immersion. We offer specialized onboarding tracks such as the Ace MT Induction and RMO Induction for Marketing, ensuring each role receives a structured and tailored foundation. 

All e-learning content is housed on our proprietary Learning Management System, Moneyversity, designed to be accessible across geographies and aligned with bestin-class learning principles. This robust ecosystem empowers our employees to learn anytime, anywhere—driving individual growth and organizational excellence.

# **KEY HIGHLIGHTS** 

## REGULATORY MATTERS 

- Unwavering commitment to regulatory compliance applicable to Middle Layer NBFCs 

- Appointed a Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) and set up a dedicated Compliance team to oversee regulatory compliance 

- Established independent Boardlevel committees for Audit, Risk, and Governance 

- Automated compliance monitoring tool deployed across 2,800+ branches 

## RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROL 

- Operates an integrated Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework aligned with RBI’s regulatory expectations 

- Risk governance is overseen by a dedicated Risk Management Committee of the Board 

- Employs Early Warning Systems and data-driven monitoring tools across portfolios 

- Comprehensive risk registers and dashboards track credit, market, operational, liquidity, and reputational risks 

- Internal control systems are designed for preventive, detective, and corrective assurance across all operations 

- Regular stress testing, scenario analysis, and back-testing validate risk appetite and capital adequacy 

- Periodic audits and risk-based internal assessments ensure alignment with internal policies and regulatory standards 

## COMMITTEES OF THE BOARD 

- The Board is supported by dedicated committees that provide focused oversight, ensure regulatory compliance, and contribute to strategic guidance 

- Several committees are chaired by Independent Directors to uphold transparency and accountability 

- Committees meet periodically as per regulatory requirements and our Company’s internal governance calendar 

## STRATEGY AND OVERSIGHT 

- The Board provides strategic direction and monitors performance against defined business objectives 

- It regularly reviews business plans, capital allocation, risk appetite, and growth priorities 

- Strategy execution is closely linked to risk-adjusted return metrics and evolving market opportunities 

- Oversight is maintained through a multi-tiered governance structure, including Board-level and management-level Committees 

- Key focus areas include digital transformation, retail-led growth, regulatory compliance excellence, and ESG integration

# BOARD OF DIRECTORS 





## **Mr. Arun Kumar Purwar Chairperson & Non-Executive Director** 

Mr. Arun Kumar Purwar is the Chairperson & Non-Executive Director of IIFL Finance Limited. He also serves as Chairman & Independent Director of Jindal Panther Cement Private Limited, Jindal Global Capability Centre Private Limited, Alkem Medtech Private Limited as well as Eroute Technologies Private Limited. He is as an Independent Director in companies across diverse sectors like Finance, Pharma, Media, Engineering consultancy, Investment Banking and Fintech sectors. He also acts as an advisor to Mizuho Securities, Japan. He was Chairman of the State Bank of India (SBI) from 2002 to 2006 and Chairman of the Indian Bank Association during 2005 to 2006. He has 

previously held positions such as Managing Director of State Bank of Patiala and was also associated in the setting up of SBI Life. Post his retirement from SBI, he was associated with a leading industry house in setting up the first healthcare-focused private equity fund as well as a non-banking finance company focused on funding real estate projects as well as educational institutions. He has won a number of awards, including the CEO of the Year Award from the Institute of Technology and Management (2004), ‘Outstanding Achiever of the Year’ Award from the Indian Banks’ Association (2004) and ‘Finance Man of the Year’ Award by the Bombay Management Association in 2006. 





## **Mr. Nirmal Jain Managing Director** 

Mr. Nirmal Jain is the Promoter and Managing Director of IIFL Finance Limited and the founder of the IIFL Group. Since founding the Group in 1995, he has led its transformation into one of India’s most respected and diversified financial services institutions. Under his leadership, the Group has established a strong presence across wealth and asset management, consumer lending, securities trading, and discount broking. IIFL today serves a rapidly expanding customer base and commands significant market capitalization across its listed entities. IIFL Finance Limited, the flagship company, is widely recognized as a leading player in India’s financial services landscape. 

Mr. Jain is widely respected for his visionary leadership and pioneering role in driving technology-led transformation in the financial sector. His emphasis on digital innovation, customer-centricity, and product excellence has fueled the Group’s consistent growth and earned the trust of marquee global investors. Beyond business, Mr. Jain is a strong advocate for financial inclusion and girl child literacy, actively working to broaden access to financial tools, education, and opportunity across India. He is also an active member and supporter of the Jain International Trade Organisation (JITO). 

Mr. Jain holds a Post Graduate Diploma in Management from the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad and is a rankholder Chartered Accountant and Cost Accountant. He began his career with Hindustan Unilever in 1989 before founding IIFL as an independent equity research firm. With over three decades of industry experience, Mr. Jain continues to play a defining role in shaping the future of financial services in India.

## **5. TRANSFER TO INVESTOR EDUCATION AND PROTECTION FUND (“IEPF”)** 

In accordance with the applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, read with the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016 (“IEPF Rules”), the Company is required to transfer all unclaimed or unpaid dividends, along with the corresponding shares 

in respect of which dividends have remained unclaimed for seven (7) consecutive years, to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF). 

Similarly, in the case of Non-Convertible Debentures (“NCDs”), the unclaimed interest and principal amounts are also required to be transferred to the IEPF Authority within thirty (30) days from the expiry of seven (7) years from the respective due dates of payment, as per the provisions of the IEPF Rules. 

During the year under review, the Company transferred `10,73,225 on April 4, 2025 being the unclaimed dividend amount, pertaining to the FY 2017-18 and has also transferred unclaimed interest and principal amount on NCDs of ` 13,90,821.68 to the IEPF. 

The shares on which dividend has not been claimed by the Members for seven (7) consecutive years shall be transferred to demat account of the IEPF Authority within thirty (30) days of expiry of the said period. Accordingly, various steps are being taken on an ongoing basis to reach out to the Shareholders, through email and other means, whose shares are due to be transferred to the IEPF, in order to create awareness and provide them an opportunity to claim their unclaimed dividends. In view of the aforesaid, the Company had also published the notice in the leading newspapers in English and Regional Language having wide circulation to inform them about the said transfer to IEPF. Post closure of the financial year, the Company, in accordance with the above provisions, transferred 8,652 equity shares to the IEPF. 

In compliance with Securities and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI”) Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHSRAC-1/P/CIR/2023/176 dated November 8, 2023, relating to unclaimed amounts in respect of listed NonConvertible Securities, the Company has put in place a procedural framework for handling unclaimed interest

## **12. INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEMS** 

## **Internal audit and its adequacy:** 

The scope and authority of the internal audit function is well defined, and to maintain independence and objectivity in its functions, the internal audit function reports directly to the Audit Committee of the Board. At the beginning of each financial year, an annual RiskBased Internal Audit (“RBIA”) plan is rolled out post approval by the Audit Committee of the Board. The audit plan aims to evaluate the efficacy and adequacy of the internal control system(s) and compliance(s) thereof, robustness of internal processes, policies and accounting procedures, compliance with laws and regulations. The internal audit function, consisting of professionally qualified accountants, engineers, fraud risk and information technology specialists, is adequately skilled and resourced to deliver audit assurances at highest levels. Based on the reports of the internal audit function, process owners undertake corrective action in their respective areas. Significant audit observations and corrective actions thereon are presented to the Audit Committee of the Board. 

## **Internal Controls over Financial Reporting:** 

Your Board is of the opinion that internal financial controls with reference to the financial statements were tested and reported adequately and operating effectively. The internal financial controls are commensurate with the size, scale and complexity of operations. The controls were tested during the year and no reportable material weaknesses either in their design or operations were observed. Your Company has put in place robust policies and procedures, which inter alia, ensure integrity in conducting its business, safeguarding of its assets, timely preparation of reliable financial information, accuracy and completeness in maintaining accounting records, prevention and detection of frauds and errors.

## **17. ANTI- BRIBERY AND ANTI-CORRUPTION POLICY** 

Your Company has an Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy (“Policy”) on combating bribery and corruption and to conduct Company’s business in an honest and ethical manner. The Company takes a zero-tolerance approach to bribery, corruption and other forms of unlawful payment (including gifts, hospitality, etc.) and are committed to act professionally, fairly and with integrity in all it’s dealings wherever it operates. The Company is also committed towards implementing and enforcing effective systems to counter bribery and corruption. The Policy prohibits offering, promising, giving or authorizing others to give anything in excess of a certain value, either directly or indirectly, to any person or entity, thereby setting out Company’s standards on bribery and other forms of unlawful payments. 

The policy provides information and guiding principles to prevent any activity or conduct relating to bribery, facilitation payments or corruption and to guide employees to act professionally, fairly and with utmost integrity in all their business dealings and relationships, wherever they operate. 

The Policy requires that the Company do not engage in bribery or corruption in any form and explicitly mentions that the Company will not pay or procure payment of a bribe or unlawful fee to encourage the performance of a task or one which is intended or likely to compromise the integrity of another. The Company will not accept any payment, gift or inducement from a third party which is intended to compromise Company’s integrity.

## **22. RISK MANAGEMENT** 

Your Company has a well-defined comprehensive Enterprise Risk Management (“ERM”) Framework in place and a robust organizational structure to identify, assess, measure and monitor risks and strengthen controls to mitigate risks. The Company has established procedures to periodically place before the Risk Management Committee and the Board, the risk assessment and minimization procedures being followed by the Company and steps taken by it to mitigate these risks. ERM has been adopted by the Company which uses defined Key Risk Indicators based on quantitative and qualitative factors. A two-dimensional quantitative heat map has been implemented, which enables the Management to have a comprehensive view of various identified risk areas based on their probability and impact. The Company have initiated adequate Risk training and awareness program to ensure preparedness. 

The composition, terms of reference and powers of the Risk Management Committee are in conformity with the requirements of Regulation 21 of the Listing Regulations and RBI SBR Direction and the same has been provided in the Corporate Governance Report. The Risk Management Committee is authorized to monitor and review overall risk management plan including liquidity risk and is also empowered, inter alia, to review and recommend to the Board the modifications to the Risk Management Policy. The ERM Policy is approved by the Board of Directors and inter alia, includes identification of risks, including strategic, financial, credit, market, liquidity, security, compliance, fraud, reputation, technology, cyber, outsourcing, people/conduct, collection, ESG, business which in the opinion of the Board may threaten the existence of the Company. 

## **23. RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS** 

Your Company has in place a Policy on Related Party Transactions (“RPTs”) (“RPT Policy”), as amended from time to time. The Policy provides for identification of RPT, necessary approvals from the Audit Committee/ Board/ Members, reporting and disclosure requirements in compliance with the provisions of the Act and Listing Regulations. The said Policy can be accessed on the website of the Company at https://storage.googleapis. com/iifl-finance-storage/files/2025-04/Policy_on_ Related_Party_Transactions_23042025.pdf. 

All contracts or arrangements executed by the 

Company during the year under review with related parties were on arm’s length basis and in the ordinary course of business. Hence, the disclosure of RPTs as required under Section 134(3)(h) of the Act, 2013 in Form AOC-2 is not applicable to the Company. 

All such RPTs were placed before the Audit Committee/ Board/Members for their approval, wherever applicable. A certificate from an Independent Chartered Accountant is placed before the Audit Committee on a quarterly basis, certifying that all related party transactions entered into by the Company during the quarter were conducted at arm’s length and in the ordinary course of business. 

You may refer to note no. 44 of the Standalone Financial Statements and note no. 44 of the Consolidated Financial Statements respectively, which contain related party disclosures. 

Your Company has obtained the Member’s approval on Material RPTs in the last AGM held on September 30, 2024 for financial year 2024-25. 

Considering that the Company is a NBFC-ML and given the nature of its business and operations, it will continue to enter into various related party transactions (RPTs) in the ordinary course of business. Accordingly, the Company has sought approval from the Members for material RPTs, the details of which are available in the Notice convening the AGM of the Company.

## **38. SIGNIFICANT & MATERIAL ORDERS PASSED BY THE REGULATORS OR COURTS OR TRIBUNALS** 

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), through a press release and order dated March 4, 2024, directed the Company to immediately cease and desist from sanctioning or disbursing gold loans, as well as from assigning, securitising, or selling any of its gold loans. However, the Company was permitted to continue servicing its existing gold loan portfolio through regular collection and recovery processes.These supervisory restrictions were imposed pending the completion of a special audit initiated by the RBI. Following the completion of the audit and RBI's inspection, the ban was lifted. 

The Special Audit commenced on April 23, 2024, and subsequently concluded, the RBI, after examining the submissions made and the remedial actions undertaken by the Company, vide its communication dated September 19, 2024, lifted the restrictions imposed on the gold loan business. The aforesaid directions were specific to the gold loan portfolio and did not affect the Company’s other business activities. The Company 

continued to operate in its other areas of business and maintains a valid NBFC license. Accordingly, there was no impact on the going concern status of the Company. 

Except for the above, no other significant or material orders have been passed by any Regulator, Court, or Tribunal that could impact the going concern status or the Company’s future operations.

## **DIVIDEND DISTRIBUTION POLICY** 

## **PURPOSE & SCOPE** 

IIFL Finance Limited (“the Company”) has in place a Board approved dividend policy covering the Company and the Subsidiaries as adopted on March 01, 2011. SEBI has mandated that the top 1000 Companies (in terms of market capitalization) need to have a Dividend Distribution Policy in place. 

Accordingly, this policy is to put into place the norms for the determination and declaration of dividend on equity capital by IIFL Finance Limited and its subsidiaries. While considering distribution and payment of dividend, the Company will ensure compliance with all the applicable provisions of the law including provisions of the Companies Act, SEBI, RBI, NHB and Income Tax Rules and Regulations etc related thereto. 

- **A. Factors/ parameters that would be considered while declaring Dividend** 

   - I. The financial parameters that shall be considered while declaring dividend 

While considering the total dividend at Holding Company and at each of the Subsidiaries the following will be taken into account: 

(including accumulated balance in P&L account) 

         - b. Profit in the any Financial Year is less than 10% of the equity capital. 

         - c. If the total income from business/ PAT from its ordinary activities in any Financial Year declines by more than 75% from the previous year 

         - d. If the business is seriously affected and visibility is uncertain. 

   - III. Internal and external factors that shall be considered for declaration of dividend: 

      - i. Internal Factors: 

         - a. Projected investment in business/new business 

         - b. Projected investments in Subsidiaries/ Associates in the year and next year. 

         - c. Networth/Capital adequacy as required under respective Regulatory requirements. 

      - ii. External Factors: 

- a. The business plan and actual performance, the capital requirements, free cash flow, debt equity ratio (considering new capital, ESOPs, retained earnings, minimum net worth requirements as per respective regulatory requirements etc.) 

- b. Adequacy of profits including the accumulated balance in Profit & Loss account and 

- c. Taxes on dividend. 

The Board may consider a higher distribution with adequate justification or on special occasions. 

- II. The circumstances under which the shareholders: 

   - i. May expect dividend: 

      - a. Surplus in Profit & loss (P&L) Statement 

      - b. Profits in any Financial Year are more than 10% of the equity capital of the Company 

   - ii. May not expect dividend: 

      - a. If there are losses as per P&L Statement 

      - a. State of Economy/Industry/business 

      - b. Statutory Taxes/levies – Changes in income tax rates, DDT etc. 

- IV. The retained earnings shall be utilized for: 

   - i. Proposed Capital expenditure 

   - ii. Investments/acquisitions 

   - iii. General corporate purposes including contingencies 

   - iv. Capital restructuring 

- V. Parameters that shall be adopted with regard to various classes of shares: The Company has only one class of equity shareholders at present. 

## **Periodicity of distribution** 

On a yearly basis, the Holding and Subsidiary Companies may distribute by way of Interim Dividend/s a substantial portion of the total dividend of the Company. The balance portion will be declared by way of final dividend considering the full year’s accounts and will be paid after the approval of shareholders at the Annual General Meeting of the Company.
